codedeployNoAutoRollback.^description: {$COUNT} CodeDeploy deployment group(s) do not automatically roll back when a deployment fails (autoRollbackConfiguration is disabled, or DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE is not among its events). Without automatic rollback a failed deployment leaves the faulty or partially applied revision running until someone intervenes manually, so a bad or tampered release stays live longer and the fleet can be left in a mixed, untested state. Enabling rollback on DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE (and, where CloudWatch alarms are configured, on DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM) returns the group to the last known good revision automatically, which is part of deploying software programmatically and repeatably.
codedeployNoAutoRollback.shortDesc: Enable automatic rollback on deployment failure
ref: [Redeploy and roll back a deployment with CodeDeploy]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-rollback-and-redeploy.html>
